correctness.rationale: Disintegrating the one-step output over its tail gives conditional first-symbol probabilities J(0x), J(1x), with the input as the tail law. Thus its entropy equals H(p)+(log 2−H(p))μ(W_q). The equal mixture of 01^∞ and 10^∞ is fair and supported on W_q. A second marker at a positive distance less than q would have its initial symbol and first tail symbol inside the constant tail of the first, impossible. At distance q its initial symbol is the final symbol of the first marker, forcing opposite type. Every length-q starting window therefore contains at most one marker, yielding mass at most 1/q by invariance. Equality makes all translated windows contain exactly one start in the two-sided stationary extension, almost surely (countably many windows); hence starts are one residue class mod q and marker types alternate. The windows determined by these markers cover the line, so the only allowed orbit is the alternating runs of length q. Uniform measure there is fair and uniquely invariant on that orbit. Since 0<p<1/2 the objective is strictly increasing in marker mass, proving uniqueness as stated. For every positive continuous normalized J, compactness bounds both branch probabilities below by a common positive δ, so the stationary fair supremum is at least H(δ)>0 (fair invariant inputs exist) and no gap can equal log 2. For p=e^{−(q+1)}, H(p)=O(qe^{−q}), proving the stated asymptotic and sharpness. The bounded independent replay `python3 -B /workspace/review-evidence/marker_overlap.py` checks every two-marker overlap length for 2≤q≤100, finding only the opposite-type one-symbol overlap; this is corroborative, not the proof over all stationary inputs.
